[BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64#2/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The argument proceeds gradually: it explains how Jesus’ life stages contradict divinity, answers doubts, invites them to mutual imprecation, then returns to an easier appeal based on Jesus, the Gospel, the prophets, and scriptures; when even that fails, it calls for public acknowledgment of Muslim faith.

[BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The shared word is a principle on which messengers and scriptures agree, and the following clauses explain it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:3:64/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Worship God alone means affirming His unity in worship and devoting worship sincerely to Him.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about priests and monks and was sent by the Prophet to Jaʿfar and his companions in Abyssinia, where Jaʿfar recited it before the Negus and Abyssinian leaders.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p193/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Most readers make سواء genitive as an adjective; al-Ḥasan reads it accusative, parsed by al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī as a verbal noun or possibly a circumstantial accusative, while the common sense is “equal.” | mentions 2:6
